newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Tabacalera sees synergies from Aldeasa buy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tabacalera sees synergies from Aldeasa buy.

text.p: Tabacalera chairman Cesar Alierta said on Wednesday he expected the group's 20 percent stake in leading duty-free shop manager Aldeasa to fit well with the Spanish tobacco firm's aim to concentrate on distribution.
"The free cash flow growth generated by (Aldeasa) will allow it to continue to finance its foreign expansion," Alierta told the annual shareholders' meeting.
"In the area of logistics, the potential synergies are evident," he added.
Stock Market Comission CNMV said that Tabacalera would buy a 20 percent stake in Aldeasa for 11.34 billion pesetas ($78 million).
It will pay an additional unspecified amount related to the price of the other 80 percent of Aldeasa, which state holding company Seppa is selling to institutions in September.
Analysts welcomed news of Tabacalera's new buy and the shares outpaced Spain's blue chip Ibex index, although some expressed caution regarding the price.

"The price is a key factor and it seems to me that Tabacalera will have to buy a premium over the price of the institutional sale, which could make the operation less attractive," one Spanish analyst said.
Officials at Tabacalera itself said they could not specify the exact price but highlighted the advantages of its link with a growing international retailer.
"Currently (Aldeasa's) expansion plans contemplate the opening of two to four shops per month. It has very attractive growth prospects," Alierta said.

"During the last three years, Aldeasa's net profit has grown an average 25 percent per year, benefiting from important increases in Spanish air traffic, from the expansion of sales space as well as the diversification of activities and international expansion," he added.
Aldeasa has an extensive retail market. It manages 100 duty-free stores in 16 Spanish airports and is present in the airports of Peru, Venezuela, Chile, Portugal and Morocco.
The tobacco maker itself is to focus on strengthening its key strategic areas of tobacco and distribution, Alierta told the meeting, and is looking at related investment opportunities abroad.

"Tabacalera at the present moment is not only studying upcoming privatisations with the aim of taking part in them but is also finalising its strategy to be present in new foreign markets( either as a vendor, a licencee or a manufacturer)," he said.
In comments to Reuters, a company official said he was not worried about the number of smokers declining in Spain and threatening the firm's profits in the future.
"There are still idiosyncracies in southern European countries which are unique. We don't think you can extrapolate (the anti-tobacco drive) in the U.S. to Latin countries," he said.
